feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter section consolidation, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong scope and relevance: web, CMS, analytics, email, social, video, governance, and AI-enabled search create a compelling senior-level digital strategy profile.  
- Good use of scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add weight and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Reduce redundancy across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; standardize serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); consider replacing “Ranked among the top public universities…” with more candidate-focused content.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and slightly less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with your current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of cross-channel leadership and transformation impact.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective large-scale communications. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” may be enough; avoid also listing public-sector/advocacy here unless tailoring for a specific role.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial operations & governance,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Group related items to reduce list fatigue and improve scanability; e.g., combine workflow/systems items and clarify “multi-channel communication” as “multi-channel communications leadership.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & systems improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Keep style consistent: use plural “communications” and parallel noun phrases throughout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Header and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only for highest-level themes.
- “Workflow design” and “systems architecture” are close enough to combine.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented position. Tighten the opening, group related work, and add concrete scale/outcomes to distinguish it from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the generic opener with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Advised,” “Delivered.”
- Add measurable context wherever possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/teams supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Example phrasing: “Led development of an AI-enabled search experience, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize consulting/embedded leadership and new AI-search/campaign work.
- Microsite and AI-search bullets also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be even stronger if the opening were tighter and more outcome-focused, with clearer separation between strategic leadership and channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize transformation and scale: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, video output, production cost savings, reporting speed, or governance efficiency.
- Make verbs more executive-level and concise: “Built” → “Launched,” “Expanded” → “Established,” “Strengthened” → “Standardized.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video channel management overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video program language may duplicate recent project/older NACo bullets; emphasize the studio build and organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination rather than broad ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on operational leadership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social, and video, scaling NACo’s editorial planning and advocacy messaging across channels.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scope: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy, and program teams around more consistent content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening line.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and footer project list.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter and more differentiated, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “transformation,” “operations,” and “stakeholder” to signal seniority and organizational impact.
- Keep terminology parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles like “audience-focused” vs. “leadership.”
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof points to recent roles rather than skills (e.g., 10,000+ page migration, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in Core Competencies; consider keeping only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section and reads more like a tool dump than a senior topline summary. For this higher-level section, emphasize platforms and modernization strengths most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to grouped, outcome-oriented capabilities: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Prioritize recent/relevant items first: put Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations ahead of older or less-evidenced platforms.
- Consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; keep them in “Technical + IT” instead.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing to “Enterprise CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for stronger senior-level positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a differentiated skills line. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and should emphasize higher-value strategic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most relevant platforms and group them tightly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI design, executive dashboards, SEO and performance analysis.”
- If space allows elsewhere, add evidence tied to recent work, e.g., “built reporting infrastructure” or “supported strategic decision-making,” but avoid forcing metrics into a skills section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “Leadership reporting” may be weaker than “executive reporting” or “executive dashboards.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps with “Core Competencies” and older NACo production work. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented to match the recent leadership profile.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize scope: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace generic bullets with tighter, higher-level phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio systems  
- Virtual event delivery and technical coordination
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: **Built and operated an in-house studio supporting advocacy programming and recurring event content**
- Keep terms consistent with recent roles: use “studio systems” and “event production” rather than only “editing” or “virtual.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “Livestream studio workflows” also appear in Technical + IT, so this section should stay strategic, not tool-based.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either add specificity or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light proficiency/context if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If you want more impact, replace this line with platform scope: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing via GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider keeping the detailed version there and shortening this item.
- Drupal is already heavily evidenced in recent roles/projects, so avoid overemphasizing it here unless you add differentiating context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation strengths that support recent Drupal, analytics, AI/search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capabilities: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3.”
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if space allows, e.g. “for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, and search/workflow enhancements.”
- Put strongest/recently used tools first: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if you want this item to stay focused on implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation and platform integration” already appears elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the strongest automation platforms first.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: “Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier”
- Use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams” for clarity and consistency with enterprise tooling.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools and may add little unless this section is explicitly for platform inventory.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Strengthen it by signaling CRM, marketing automation, and member communications relevance tied to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers for relevance: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (CRM + marketing automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- If you have credible scope, consider one short impact cue elsewhere in the CV, not here: e.g., “managed newsletter programs reaching tens of thousands” to connect tools to outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about email/newsletters; keep this entry tool-focused only.
- Avoid adding analytics terms here; those are already covered well under “Data, Analytics & Optimization.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” scale, and team-building contributions from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/reach of weekly videos, or workflow improvements (faster publishing, more consistent output, reduced vendor reliance).
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft verbs like “supporting,” “contributed,” and “high-impact”; use “built,” “launched,” “produced,” “streamlined,” “supervised.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, strengthened cross-channel publishing workflows, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launch/build phase rather than ongoing ownership.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video” language already used more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; produced digital and multimedia content to extend project visibility and member engagement.”
- Add a stronger second sentence: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Tighten wording by removing generic phrases like “organizational programs and policy work” unless you can specify policy areas or internal clients.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here; later NACo roles already cover video, livestreams and digital operations in more depth.
- “Launched the organization’s first podcast” is the clearest differentiator—keep that central.
